mission: The group discovers Jacen’s cache was hidden in old offworld survey/GAG storage equipment near the Glasswell, not in a mystical altar. Talon recognizes the storage logic. Ben recognizes the Force wrongness. Sela recognizes the local danger. When they get close enough to scan the outer data layers, Ben confirms what Iressa told them in her dying transmission at the Midpoint: the holocron is unfinished, containing Jacen’s work on Recognition and Holding — exactly the identity-shaping techniques the Vigil intends to weaponize with Aevyn’s help. The SPP function here is embodiment rather than revelation. Ben already knew (from Iressa) what the holocron was for. Seeing the cache, seeing Aevyn already at work on it, makes the threat concrete. There is no way to stop Aevyn from getting at the holocron cleanly. The only options left are rescue (saving Tavi and the locals from what Aevyn’s work is about to break) and denial (keeping Aevyn from leaving with the full prize).
why_now: The heavy equipment is moving and the Glasswell is already destabilizing — waiting for a better moment to enter means there is no moment and no Tavi.
conflict: Iressa told Ben what the holocron contained. Seeing Aevyn already at work on the cache makes it real in a way the dying transmission never quite did — and the cache being in ordinary GAG survey equipment, not a Sith altar, is somehow worse, because it means Jacen planned this practically and calmly.
turning_point: Aevyn begins forcing the cache open. The Glasswell starts to answer.
closing_hook: Aevyn begins forcing the cache open. The Glasswell starts to answer.
setting: Iresh, the Glasswell upper chamber — the entrance to the cavern system beneath the mirror-lake. Pale translucent mineral walls, faintly luminescent. Old offworld survey equipment and a concealed GAG-era storage container near the cache site. Aevyn is already at work when the group arrives. Iresh sits on the wild edge near the Kathol Rift — Jacen chose it for that reason, a waypoint on the Force odyssey that took him to the Aing-Tii and back. The world is as ordinary as the container; the choice was deliberate.
emotional_trajectory: Make Jacen feel like Jacen: mystical insight plus cold logistics. The cache being in old survey equipment is the right Jacen-shaped detail. Ben’s reaction to confirming Iressa was right should be quiet — not horror, but the kind of bracing that comes when a worst case becomes the actual case. Reader-onboarding / grounding note: The Glasswell is not a Sith temple, Jedi ruin, or treasure chamber. It is a natural site Jacen exploited with practical concealment. Plain-language consequence of the SPP confirmation: Aevyn is already cracking it; we are too late to stop him from getting at it; the question now is whether we can save anyone caught underneath, and whether we can deny him the part that matters most.

stakes.personal: The cache is in a decommissioned GAG-era survey container — the same administrative category of equipment Talon handled after Tess moved him into records/logistics. Ben recognizes the model. It is the exact kind of ordinary object Jacen would have used to hide something extraordinary, and recognizing it means Ben understands how Jacen thought.
stakes.interpersonal: Talon reads the storage logic before Ben names it: 'That's a GAG quarantine container. Survey clearance, standard field rotation. Nobody opens those.' It is not pride in his old knowledge; it is the specific misery of recognizing how you were used.
stakes.external: Aevyn is already applying the Recognition technique to the container — the Glasswell is starting to answer the pressure, and the upper chamber walls are showing the first hairline stress fractures. They are not too late, but they are very close to too late.

sensory_details: The upper Glasswell chamber: pale translucent mineral walls that catch ambient light and hold it faintly, luminescent against the dark below. The survey container is half-embedded in a mineral ledge — no markings, no decals, exactly the right kind of boring. The Glasswell's ambient resonance is audible as a low sustained hum that Ben can feel in his back teeth. Aevyn does not look up when they enter. One concrete anchor: Talon names the container model before Ben does — standard GAG quarantine-survey rotation, the kind that never gets inspected at a field site on the far edge near the Rift. Ben's recognition is a beat behind Talon's because Talon handled the logistics. What hits Ben is the odyssey-logic underneath: Jacen routed this to Iresh because Iresh is a waypoint, close enough to Kathol Rift space that the Aing-Tii's resonance reaches the place.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Aevyn begins forcing the Recognition technique at higher intensity — not reading the container's ordinary surface, but making it remember the specific moment Jacen sealed it. The Glasswell amplifies the pressed impression. The upper chamber hum shifts in pitch and the first crack appears along the mineral shelf above the lower approach.
turning_point_detail.shift: The group realizes simultaneously that the Glasswell is not simply a location for the cache — Aevyn's technique is destabilizing the cavern structure itself. They are not watching a safe extraction; they are watching the beginning of a collapse.
turning_point_detail.cost: They cannot stop Aevyn from getting into the cache cleanly. The only options are rescue — getting Tavi and anyone else below out before the water comes — and denial — keeping Aevyn from leaving with the full prize. Neither option includes preventing the collapse.

emotional_arc.start: Ben enters the Glasswell upper chamber already running contingency plans — if Aevyn is this far along, what are the options?
emotional_arc.shift: Seeing the cache in person, in ordinary GAG survey equipment, lands the quiet confirmation Iressa's transmission never quite delivered. She was right. It is real. This is what Jacen left.
emotional_arc.end: Ben braces rather than reacts. Iressa died telling him what this was. He does not get to be surprised by it. He gets to figure out what to do next.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben, Talon, and Sela enter the Glasswell upper chamber and find Aevyn already at work on the survey container — not theatrically, just a man doing a difficult technical task.
key_beats.state_change: They arrive too late to prevent the opening; what remains is the question of what they can still interrupt or deny.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the flat recognition that his timing was wrong; contingency thinking starting before the surprise registers

key_beats.beat_description: Talon identifies the container model immediately and names what it means: standard GAG survey clearance, the kind no inspector opens during a quarantine sweep.
key_beats.state_change: The cache's concealment method is understood — ordinary administrative camouflage, Jacen's specific kind of practical.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the quiet arrival of confirmation — she was right, Iressa was right, it is exactly as ordinary as Jacen would have made it

key_beats.beat_description: Ben confirms through the Force that this is the cache Iressa described — Recognition and Holding, unfinished, Jacen's private laboratory work.
key_beats.state_change: The worst case is now the actual case — the threat Iressa died naming is real and in front of him.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the bracing rather than the reaction; no room to be surprised, only to calculate what comes next

key_beats.beat_description: Aevyn applies sustained Recognition pressure to force the container's seal; the Glasswell amplifies and the first crack appears in the upper chamber wall.
key_beats.state_change: The extraction is actively destabilizing the structure — this is no longer a safe extraction scenario.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the shift from threat-assessment to emergency-assessment; the sound of the crack landing before the visual does

key_beats.beat_description: The group understands simultaneously that the collapse is already beginning below where Tavi is and that stopping Aevyn cleanly is no longer an option.
key_beats.state_change: The mission forks into rescue and denial — neither includes preventing the collapse.
key_beats.pov_reaction: the narrowing of options felt as physical compression; the triage starting before he names it aloud

canon_elements_needed: Iresh physical geography and local survival rules
Kathol Rift as Jacen's Force-odyssey waypoint: Iresh sits near it; that proximity is why the site was chosen, not accident
Aing-Tii flow-walking as the technique underlying Recognition — Ben recognizes the odyssey in the container's placement the way Talon recognizes the storage model

Drafter texture cue: two parallel recognitions land in the same beat — Talon reads the GAG storage logic (he handled these containers in records/logistics), Ben reads the odyssey-logic (Jacen chose a world near the Kathol Rift on purpose). One term per character, one consequence per character: Talon's consequence is the specific misery of seeing how he was used; Ben's consequence is understanding that Jacen planned this Force journey with the same calm he planned everything else. Do not merge the two recognitions into a single reaction. Keep them separate and sequential.
